mainText: This is Dose of Good for Wednesday, November 25. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Kiwi return to Wellington's hills after more than 150 years. More than 250 kiwi have been reintroduced since 2022 in a Māori-led project, and the population now exceeds 300 birds, including wild-hatched chicks. With over 5,300 predator traps, chick survival is above 90%. Second: Bacteria-carrying mosquitoes cut dengue infections by 68% in Brazilian city. A study of 5,757 children aged 6 to 11 in Belo Horizonte found that releasing Aedes aegypti mosquitoes carrying Wolbachia bacteria cut dengue infections by 68.5% and chikungunya by 73.3%. The research is led by UFMG with Fiocruz and the World Mosquito Program. Third: High-school students become air-pollution monitors in São Paulo. Students at a technical school in São Paulo measured air quality for 10 months, gathering 2,100 valid readings. They wrote a booklet proposing more green space and dust control, and the work was published in a scientific journal. Fourth: Brazilian AI improves identification of stars, galaxies and quasars. Researchers at the University of São Paulo combined 1.5 million simulated objects with real observations to train a model. Its accuracy at finding distant quasars rose from 0.40 to 0.68, helping large sky surveys such as J-PAS. Fifth: Court secures quilombola applicant's place in medical school selection. A federal appeals court ruled unanimously that self-declaration and a Palmares Foundation certificate are enough to secure an application from the Portão do Gelo quilombo in Olinda to the university's medicine selection. The university had rejected it for lacking another document. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
